analysis: The closest option gives direct weight to film form, documentary, media archaeology, race and representation, television and digital media, and environmental communication. Replacing two adjacent literature and heritage courses with media and environment and television makes this stronger. Sociology and history supply context and research, while literature and visual art support interpretation.

The film option retains film form, documentary and adaptation. Literary sources, visual heritage, museums and rhetoric shift the organising question to how stories and visual objects are interpreted and presented. Archaeology contributes interpretation of material objects, not film archival practice. The option does not claim studio or production-specialist equivalence.

The television option uses From T.V. to TikTok for direct study of television and digital representation. Communicating the Climate Crisis, applied rhetoric, persuasion and social research methods develop questions about public communication and audiences. Research and statistics provide empirical tools, not a specialist television audience analytics curriculum. Replaced leadership and market research with direct television study and applied rhetoric, and moved Modern Sociology to its offered term.

Paired only supported overlaps in audiovisual form, media change, documentary practice, film analysis and qualitative methods. UvA retains its own history, theory, production, restricted choices and thesis. Optional UCR independent research stays separate from scheduled credits.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics

GOSHIST111.name: Modern History

GOSHIST312.name: Researching the “American Century”
GOSHIST312.contribution: Builds a historical research project on the American century through question design and critical source analysis.

GOSPHIL111.name: Introduction to Western Philosophy
GOSPHIL111.contribution: Reads philosophical arguments from ancient and modern traditions to develop contextual interpretation and reasoned critique.

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics

GOSPHIL311.name: Philosophy of Emotion

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: Develops ethically grounded qualitative research design, data collection, analysis and communication.

GOSSOCI214.name: Modern Sociology

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods

MCCCOMM111.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
MCCCOMM111.contribution: Analyses argument, rhetorical form and delivery, with practice in persuasive communication.

MCCCOMM211.name: Style & Meaning
MCCCOMM211.contribution: Analyses how grammar, deixis and other linguistic choices shape effects in literary and nonfiction texts.

MCCCOMM212.name: Communicating the Climate Crisis
MCCCOMM212.contribution: Examines public communication of climate issues through texts, film, exhibitions, protest art and social media.

MCCCOMM213.name: Rhetoric in Action
MCCCOMM213.contribution: Develops and adapts public-speaking, storytelling and debating activities with primary-school children.

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: Evaluates framing, argument and ethical persuasion, applying these to community-engaged work.

MCCCOMM312.name: Creative Communication Laboratory
MCCCOMM312.contribution: Uses poetry, performance and experimental practice to explore and communicate artistic ideas.

MCCHEAM111.name: Introduction to Western Art History
MCCHEAM111.contribution: Relates Western visual art from the late medieval period to contemporary practice to religious, political and cultural change.

MCCHEAM112.name: Introduction to World Archaeology
MCCHEAM112.contribution: Interprets artefacts and production practices to study how objects shaped communities and identities across ancient societies.

MCCHEAM211.name: African Art & Heritage
MCCHEAM211.contribution: Examines African visual traditions, their cultural meanings and the interpretation and display of heritage.

MCCHEAM212.name: Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean
MCCHEAM212.contribution: Studies Renaissance Italian art and architecture through artistic exchanges across the Mediterranean.

MCCHEAM312.name: Modern Art & Modern Museums
MCCHEAM312.contribution: Connects modern and contemporary artworks to museums, exhibitions and the institutions that shape public reception.

MCCHEAM316.name: Writing Art's Histories
MCCHEAM316.contribution: Critiques how art historians have interpreted visual culture and constructed the discipline over time.

MCCLITR111.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
MCCLITR111.contribution: Uses close reading and genre to interpret fiction, poetry, drama and nonfiction, with an introduction to film adaptation.

MCCLITR112.name: Great Literary Works
MCCLITR112.contribution: Compares major literary works across periods through questions of freedom, gender, community and mortality.

MCCLITR211.name: World Myth & Literature
MCCLITR211.contribution: Compares mythic narratives across traditions and studies their transmission and treatment of power, love and gender.

MCCLITR212.name: Life & Travel Writing
MCCLITR212.contribution: Examines how memoir, travel writing and digital self-presentation construct memory and identity.

MCCLITR311.name: Film & Text
MCCLITR311.contribution: Compares how literary narratives and their film adaptations use their different forms to tell stories.

MCCLITR312.name: Perspectives on Literary Meaning
MCCLITR312.contribution: Applies theories of reading and interpretation to a literary research project.

MCCMEDI111.name: Introduction to Film & Media
MCCMEDI111.contribution: Uses editing, sound, cinematography, narrative and performance to explain how moving images create meaning.

MCCMEDI112.name: Media Archaeology
MCCMEDI112.contribution: Interprets communication technologies from print and early recording to networks as historical and cultural objects.

MCCMEDI211.name: From T.V. to TikTok
MCCMEDI211.contribution: Studies power, social history and representation in US television, film and contemporary digital media.

MCCMEDI212.name: Media & the Environment
MCCMEDI212.contribution: Analyses how media shape ecological understanding and how people represent human and nonhuman relationships.

MCCMEDI311.name: Media & Race
MCCMEDI311.contribution: Investigates race, representation and power through American media and popular culture.

MCCMEDI312.name: The Documentary
MCCMEDI312.contribution: Studies the ethics, aesthetics and history of nonfiction representation and develops practical documentary work.

alignment.rationale: Both analyse how narrative, sound and image produce meaning. UvA applies these tools across a wider range of media objects.
Both examine historical changes in media technologies and their cultural effects. UCR studies the material history of media from print to digital networks.
Both include practical documentary production. UvA also covers fiction production and its associated workflows.
Both use close analysis of film form. UCR centres on adaptations, while UvA also uses frameworks such as auteur, genre and spectator theory.
Both develop research design and qualitative interpretation. UCR applies these methods to social questions, while UvA includes methods and sources specific to media.
